speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have three supplementary questions in this regard.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First, are the participation rates at the CGS Drive, or the CGS Day, to NEA's satisfaction?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How can NEA further cultivate greater interest and involvement of our Singaporeans towards the objectives that we have set in relation to CGS?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And finally, whether NEA can consider, as part of the annual celebrations at the CGS Day, to consider setting some targets or begin to start tracking in relation to how much carbon footprint reductions, energy waste efforts reductions we have been doing in the community?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On the day itself, we can, then, present and share with fellow Singaporeans the powerfulness of the community coming together to do green and go green.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But CGS is a movement, and it involves a large number of events across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The number of stakeholders, non-governmental organisations and community groups has also been increasing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we do indeed track participation, but it is not so clear what the correct number to target is for any given event.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: At each event, you may do it one year, you may not do it the next year, depending on the needs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think the key thing is that, overall, the awareness of the need for reduce, reuse and recycle, the interest from stakeholders in stepping forward and the participation of the public in these sustainability efforts is what is important – rather than necessarily whether the number of people at any given event increasing every year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In actual fact, the number of people participating in CGS and NEA-related events each year has, indeed, increased.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But that is not necessarily the absolute target that we should strive for.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: How can NEA cultivate further interest and engagement?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And all of this is towards the idea of increasing interest and engagement in initiatives that can help us to reduce, reuse, recycle, and improve our sustainability.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The idea of looking at carbon savings and energy savings around each event is an interesting one.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It sometimes takes quite a lot of effort to be able to do so.
